Description: Cross-cloud IAM misconfiguration leads to unauthorized data access or breach
Treatment Actions: Implement unified IAM baseline across AWS and Azure (CTL-008); Enable continuous posture monitoring / CSPM (CTL-010); Enforce MFA and JIT elevation for cloud admin roles (CTL-004, CTL-005)

Description: Weak RBAC on CRM leads to unauthorized access to merchant/customer data
Treatment Actions: CRM RBAC review; remove over-permissioned roles (CTL-004); Enforce MFA for all CRM users and admins (CTL-004); Encrypt CRM exports and apply masking (CTL-028)

Description: Firewall rule misconfiguration allows network intrusion
Treatment Actions: Quarterly firewall rule review and baseline update (CTL-008); Integrate firewall logging with SIEM (CTL-010); Patch firmware vulnerabilities (CTL-009)

Description: Fraud scoring model exhibits bias or performance drift, producing unfair or inaccurate decisions
Treatment Actions: Operate drift-monitoring dashboard with defined thresholds (CTL-018); Track fairness metrics on a defined cadence (CTL-015); Quarterly HITL model review (CTL-016)

Description: Underwriting model produces disparate impact against a protected class
Treatment Actions: Complete disparate-impact testing on current model version (CTL-015); Publish adverse-action rationale for all declines (CTL-017); Underwriter sign-off retained as HOTL control (CTL-016)

Description: Third-party LLM copilot leaks customer PII through prompts sent to the external vendor
Treatment Actions: Deploy PII scanning/redaction on prompts before vendor transmission (CTL-021); Confirm DPA terms restrict vendor training on Solidian Pay data (CTL-019); Record the vendor transfer in the disclosure register (CTL-025)

Description: Foundation-model vendor deprecates or materially changes a model version without adequate notice, breaking production copilots
Treatment Actions: Contractual deprecation-notice requirement (CTL-019); Maintain fallback/secondary model option for critical paths; Assess vendor concentration risk at annual review (CTL-037)

Description: Incomplete data lineage in the ML training pipeline obscures the source of biased or low-quality training data
Treatment Actions: Complete data lineage mapping for all production model training sets (CTL-020); Institute data quality sampling audits (CTL-020)

Description: Incomplete or inaccurate transaction processing results in settlement breaks, duplicate or dropped payments, and breach of processing-integrity service commitments
Treatment Actions: Daily reconciliation between processing ledger and settlement records with documented sign-off (CTL-035); Automated input validation and file-completeness checks at batch ingestion (CTL-035); Exception queue aging thresholds with escalation to Payment Operations lead (CTL-035)

Description: Processing capacity is exceeded during peak settlement windows, causing transactions to miss committed processing timelines
Treatment Actions: Capacity forecasting ahead of peak settlement windows (CTL-027); SLO alerting on processing latency against committed timelines (CTL-027); Communicate processing commitments and failure-reporting channel to merchants (CTL-031)

Description: Personal information is disclosed to a third party without a documented legal basis or record of the disclosure
Treatment Actions: Maintain disclosure register covering all third-party PII disclosures (CTL-025); Transfer impact assessments and executed DPAs for US/Canada/UK flows (CTL-025); Privacy commitments embedded in vendor contracts at onboarding (CTL-026)
